title: Admin - Content Management - Display Page Status - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Content Management - Display Page Status feature on the Y4J platform. This feature displays publishing status labels (Published/Draft) on each informational page in the admin panel. Published pages are visible to users while Draft pages remain internal. Covers status display, visibility rules, consistency, and edge cases.

testCases.title: Pages display status labels in the page list
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content Management page is loaded with at least one page.
steps: Verify each page entry shows a status label
expectedResults: Each page in the list displays a status label
The status label is clearly visible (e.g., badge, tag, or text)
Status labels are either 'Published' or 'Draft'
No page is missing a status label
testCases.postconditions: Status labels are confirmed visible on all pages

testCases.title: Published status label is displayed correctly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. At least one published page exists.
expectedResults: The page shows 'Published' as its status label
The label is visually distinct (e.g., green badge or specific styling)
The label text is readable and unambiguous
The status accurately reflects the page's publishing state
testCases.postconditions: Published status is confirmed displayed correctly

testCases.title: Draft status label is displayed correctly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. At least one draft page exists.
expectedResults: The page shows 'Draft' as its status label
The label is visually distinct from 'Published' (e.g., different color or style)
The label text is readable and unambiguous
The status accurately reflects the page's draft state
testCases.postconditions: Draft status is confirmed displayed correctly

testCases.title: Published pages are visible to end users
testCases.preconditions: A page with 'Published' status exists. The page has a known slug/URL.
steps: Note the slug of a published page
Open a new browser/incognito window (as a regular user)
Navigate to the page URL using the slug
expectedResults: The published page is accessible to regular users
The page content is displayed correctly
No login is required to view published pages
The page loads without errors

testCases.title: Draft pages are NOT visible to end users
testCases.preconditions: A page with 'Draft' status exists. The page has a known slug/URL.
steps: Note the slug of a draft page
Open a new browser/incognito window (as a regular user)
Navigate to the page URL using the slug
expectedResults: The draft page is NOT accessible to regular users
A 404 error or 'Page not found' message is shown
OR the user is redirected away from the draft page
No draft content is exposed to non-admin users
testCases.postconditions: Draft pages are confirmed hidden from public

testCases.title: Draft pages are visible in admin panel
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Draft pages exist.
steps: Navigate to Content Management page as Admin
Verify draft pages are visible in the admin list
expectedResults: Draft pages are visible in the admin Content Management list
They show 'Draft' status label
Admins can see, edit, and manage draft pages
Draft pages are only hidden from public users, not admins
testCases.postconditions: Draft pages are accessible to admins

testCases.title: Status labels are consistent after page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Pages with various statuses are displayed.
steps: Note the status of each page in the list
expectedResults: After refresh, all status labels remain the same
No status changes occur without admin action
Statuses are loaded from the backend (not cached incorrectly)
The display is consistent and reliable
testCases.postconditions: Status labels are consistent across refreshes

testCases.title: Status updates correctly when page is published
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A draft page exists.
steps: Publish the page (via edit or publish action)
Observe the status label after publishing
expectedResults: The status label changes from 'Draft' to 'Published'
The change is reflected immediately in the list
The page becomes accessible to public users
No page refresh is required to see the status change
testCases.postconditions: Status updates to Published after publishing

testCases.title: Status labels are visually distinguishable from each other
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Both Published and Draft pages exist.
steps: Observe a Published page status label
Observe a Draft page status label
expectedResults: 'Published' and 'Draft' labels are visually different (different colors, icons, or styles)
An admin can quickly distinguish between the two statuses at a glance
The distinction does not rely solely on color (text is different too)
Both labels are readable and clear

testCases.title: Status is displayed on paginated pages
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page list has multiple pages (pagination).
expectedResults: Status labels are displayed on all pages of the list
Each page entry shows its correct status regardless of pagination
No status labels are missing on subsequent pages

testCases.title: Status is displayed when search/filter is applied
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Search or filter functionality exists.
steps: Verify status labels are still visible
expectedResults: Status labels remain visible on filtered/searched results
Filtering does not hide or break the status display
Each filtered page shows its correct status
testCases.postconditions: Status labels display correctly with filters
